worked: The high-stakes opening statement and hook text ('193 MPH CRASH') drove strong reach, securing 1,215 views and 43.3 views per hour at 28 hours, beating the majority of earlier benchmark Shorts (which dropped as low as 190 views and 7.6 views per hour).
hurt: Engagement collapsed to 1.3 likes per 100 views (16 likes total) and 0 comments, the lowest engagement rate in the dataset where previous videos ranged from 2.0 to 7.9 likes per 100 views, caused by three straight beats of generic launch exposition that stalled the crash payoff before ending on an awkward circular loop.
diagnosis.change_next: Eliminate the middle exposition beats about launch history and move directly from the opening crash to the human blunder: follow 'A $264 million NASA spacecraft smashed into the desert' immediately with 'It happened because four gravity switches were installed completely upside down,' and replace the repetitive looping final beat with a sharp, punchy resolution about the rescued samples.
